eligibility.quote: I just updated my Groovy debian installation with the release that was posted today on ros-users and now collada meshes no longer appear in RViz.  In particular, the TurtleBot is now basically invisible.
eligibility.reason: The independently released viewer changed its interpretation of a mesh declaration consumed from another package. Wrong scale crosses the model/viewer boundary; changing the unit declaration is neither deployment wiring nor build-only. The observed operation is UPGRADE.

failed_conditions.reason: This hunk is in create_description/meshes/create_body.dae. The resource's declared unit, rather than a message definition or nominal type, is the mismatch.

loudness.quote: Actually, it doesn't look like scaling, but it is pretty messed up on my machine as well (whole robot is just a few speckles of gray and white scattered around)
loudness.reason: Visual failure is reported, not a loader diagnostic.

detection_stage.quote: In particular, the TurtleBot is now basically invisible.

resolution.quote: turtlebot_create version 2.0.1 fixes this issue. It's now available on shadow-fixed.
resolution.reason: The release/fix statement is not an observation of the specified resolved pair. The earlier successful scale workaround used the reporter's own older meshes, explicitly not guaranteed to match the packaged meshes.

notes: Read turtlebot#65 and rviz#622 with all comments, rviz#603, turtlebot_create#7 and its empty comments list, and merge 9299530's diff. Other robot meshes mentioned in rviz#622 do not add conditions to the selected create_body composition. rviz#603 says: 'This patch introduces the ability to read the unit scaling factor from Collada mesh resources.'
